title: 물건을 잃어버렸어요: 어디에 두고 왔어요?
objective: By the end, you can say what you lost and where you left or put it, and understand a short conversation about looking for a lost item.
summary: Learn ten everyday words for losing, leaving behind, and finding your things in Korea.

task.title: Use the lost-item words
task.line: Read each item, then choose, fill in, order, or write the Korean words from this worksheet.

words.exampleMeaning: I lost my umbrella on the subway.

words.meaning: to find (here); also 'to look for' (뭐 찾아요? = What are you looking for?)
words.exampleMeaning: I found my phone! It was under the sofa.

words.meaning: to look in a place for something, to check

words.exampleMeaning: All my cards are in my wallet.
I don't have my key, so I can't get into my house.
I put my phone on the desk.
I left my laptop at the office.

words.meaning: to go missing, to be gone

words.exampleMeaning: I usually keep my key in my pocket.
Try calling the lost and found.

exercises: Choose the word that fits: ① 집에 못 들어가요. ____가 없어요. (열쇠 / 지갑) ② 돈을 못 내요. ____이 없어요. (열쇠 / 지갑)
Fill in each blank with 잃어버렸어요 or 찾았어요: ① 어제 버스에서 장갑을 ____. ② 오늘 분실물 센터에서 그 장갑을 ____.
Fill in the blank with the past form of 놓다: 안경을 침대 옆에 ____.
Read and answer Yes or No: 가: 뭐 찾아요? 나: 지갑이요. 주머니에 없어요. 가: 가방도 찾아봤어요? 나: 네, 가방에도 없어요. ① The wallet is in 나's pocket. ② 나 already looked in the bag.
Put the words in the right order to make a sentence: 없어졌어요 / 가방에서 / 지갑이
You left your umbrella at a café. Finish the sentence with 두고 오다 in the past: 카페에 우산을 ____.
answers: 가방에서 지갑이 없어졌어요. (also: 지갑이 가방에서 없어졌어요.)
